source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 6 June 1952, p. 5 ("County and rural council elections: results"); Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10 ("County and rural council nominations")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the 23 electoral divisions of Limavady rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Twenty-seven candidates were nominated and four divisions were contested; the Nationalists gained two seats and with them control of the council. Sixteen of the nineteen unopposed members added from the nominations report (Derry Journal, 21 May 1952, p. 2; Londonderry Sentinel, 22 May 1952, p. 2): Ballykelly as the report gives it, the rest from their divisions at the 1949 return. Aghanloo, Feeny and The Highlands (W. J. Thompson, James O'Kane, John Alcorn) are held, as for 1949 (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Nationalist gain from the Unionists.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Drumreighland' to Drumraighland (13 Nov 2026, by the owner's rule for division spellings: the official or DED-map name where there is one, otherwise the spelling most rounds use): the DED maps of 1930-69 (DRUMRAIGHLAND) spell it Drumraighland. This round was filed under the spelling 'Drumreighland', a form of the division's name it keeps as an alias; the old address (drumreighland) answers with a redirect to this one.
